institutionName: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Far away as well as Hong Kong being an interesting place to me as well as being very different from Copenhagen. The University also had many interesting looking courses within my field. With this university I also had the opportunity to go with my girlfriend, which also weighted a bit. Another thing is the facilities and beautiful location of the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I don't remember there being any problems.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There where introduction seminars as well as flyers and mails. I also had a very good exchange buddy.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: All exchange student had their orientation together. So easy to meet the other exchange students. I would have liked to have had some introduction events with my line of study to be introduced to the locals and the exchange students within my studies, although you are not really connected to a spsecific study.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You were assigned a dorm room to be shared with another exchange student.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Quite poor cooking facilities. There were a few stoves, but you would need your own pans, plates, cutlery etc. There is no food clubs as known from Danish dorms or any real socializing in the common areas/kitchen. I just ate in the canteens which were quite okay in quality and price.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Very nice with the free sports facilities everywhere. The rooms are not that big or nice. The bathroom facilities could also be nicer. There is not much socializing within the dorms. You have to sign in guests and they can only visit between 9-23. You cant drink in the dorms at all... For me it felt more like I was living in a hostel for 4 months, rather than it being my home...

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Available courses for the semester is announced only about a month before the semester start. There is no exam dates or description available. Exam dates are announced halfway through the semester and the exams are purely run by the professors, so you have to ask them for details on the exam. For many courses their are also much grading during the semester and mid-terms. You can only get that information from the course.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
It is all through their online system, but it is a bit confusing at first and it all happens a couple of days before the semester start until two weeks into the semester. I am not sure I remember it completely. 
In the beginning there is a period were you can add courses to a wish list. If their are any prerequisites or if it is a post-graduate course and you are undergrad you have have to apply for approval with the professor. Then their is a period were you actually sign up for the approved courses. After the semester starts you can add/drop/swap courses for two weeks. You might be pre-approved and signed up for courses you have listed in the application process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online guides.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Didn't get one course because the approval came after the course was full.. Worked fine with other courses. It seems quite a few professors are away on vacation when the course registration starts, so a few approvals came quite late.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Send the approval asap. They don't have to be very detailed. I suspect they don't look that closely at them. Get approved for all courses you are interested in. In the add/drop period (the first two weeks) most courses have no assignments and all lectures are purely introductory, so use it to find out which courses you want as their is quite little information available, it is easy to swap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The academic level is not above KU and maybe even slightly below. The workload is about the same, but the workload distribution is very poor. It is very slow in the beginning, almost stressingly slow. After the spring break, all courses starts during more assignments, final projects, some still have mid-terms and then the exams come. I still had assignments during the exam period... The last month can be very stressful, especially if you have higher level courses, I think, as I had since I am a Msc student at KU and could max take two year 3 or below courses. 
Another thing is that most courses are bad at giving any feedback other than a final score as well as most also are very slow at grading the assignment. The grading at the university is relative (I think that is the norm for Hong Kong), meaning your grade is based on how well the other students did, which adds to the stress, especially since they are so bad at grading. So you have no idea how well you are actually doing. It also sets up a environment for competition. They nickname the university: UST=university of stress and tension. Luckily as an exchange student my impression is that it is not difficult to pass, but it is difficult to know how well you are doing as it doesn't depend on your performance alone.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had one year 3 course, three year 4 courses and a year five (post-grad). The post-grad course may have had the lowest workload. The academic level is slightly below KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more focus on lectures, which were of generally much poorer quality than KU. Mostly done on power points. The slides (lecture notes as they called them) is their most important course material even though most were not that good. Their TA session are a joke. If there is a TA session it is only 50 minutes a week. The ones I have had, has been a TA going through some computer program or method at a lecture room or walking (very fast due to the tome) through solutions to exercises. You don't get to sit down with the exercises yourself with the TA being available to help you, which is what I am used to from KU. The TA is there to tell you how do it, not help you learn it, but that is most likely a cultural thing.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CENG5840: Nanomaterials for Chemical Engineering Applications. 
CHEM4420: Statistical Machine Learning Methods for Chemical Data Analysis.
LIFS4320: Data Science for Biology and Medicine
MATH4335: Introduction to Optimization
PHYS3142: Computational Methods in Physics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
CHEM4420: Teaching is not the best, but it is very chill and the professor is very friendly. You only have to do a project in the end. 
PHYS3142: If you can already program in python it will be quite easy. The workload is quite high with an assignment each week and an exam projects. The bar for passing is quite low though, the professor said he passes all that has at least tried to do all assignments. It is also decadently taught.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Had to buy a new computer.... Computers are much cheaper than in DK.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Many Groceries are more expensive than DK. Restaurants are generally cheaper than DK. A meal in the canteen is 25-40 kr. Public transport it very good and cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very cool with the many free to use sports facilities and the booking is very easy. Difficult to get into a club/sports courses.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were some student clubs. Didn't participate

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do sports and go hike in the beautiful HK nature

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Macau for a day. Didn't go to mainland China as it was still difficult to get in, but it might get better. Travel South East Asia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: No too bad. There is some stuff that is difficult to get used to, fx a different socially accepted behaviors.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No, it is quite difficult I think. They are very shy and often surprisingly bad at English considering everything at the university is in english.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Teaching style. Different socially accepted behaviors.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food. I mostly appreciated experiencing the culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't worry too much about the relative grading. Sign up for as many exchange intro activities as possible. Explore the nature - go hiking.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for a student octopus card asap.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Trying something completely different.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Befriending locals, adjusting to and accepted the teaching style.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It is a cool campus with beautiful location in the mountains and down by the water. The on-campus facitlities are mostly good with many restaurants , McDonalds, super market, 7-11, sports facilities etc. The transportation to and from the city could have been easier as the metro doesn't go all the way to campus.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
